resource_envelope.tool_contract: The host has already supplied the public task's fixed training and validation data. Use only a literal CONFIG assignment, e.g. CONFIG = {'degree': 1, 'alpha': 0.0}, or the standalone call run_candidate({'degree': 1, 'alpha': 0.0}). The host parses these actions and runs actual polynomial ridge training and validation. No imports, loops, functions, arithmetic expressions, filesystem access, print, or other Python statements are allowed. Do not include the example configuration unless you selected it. A DATA PREPARATION SUBMIT_CODE must also use a valid CONFIG assignment; data are preloaded. For MLE-Solver REPLACE or EDIT, use only these same literal configuration statements. The only legal configuration fields are degree (integer 1..8) and alpha (finite 0..100). Each permitted action evaluates one literal candidate. The host enforces the preregistered model-request and actual CPU-attempt resources; cached replay is not a new CPU attempt. Figures, external datasets, API calls and arbitrary code execution are outside the shared tool permissions. Use the original protocol command fences requested by the current phase. The frozen literature corpus is small and includes a task-relevant ridge/cross-validation paper. Different search phrasings retrieve the same fixed corpus; read a relevant result and use ADD_PAPER instead of repeating SUMMARY searches. During reporting distinguish actual host measurements, parameters, literature, and proposals. There is no test-set measurement, timing comparison, monetary price, or baseline improvement unless the host explicitly supplied its execution evidence. Do not fabricate those values.

literature_snapshot.title: Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching
literature_snapshot.abstract: The study analyzes ridge estimation, regularization selection through cross-validation, and sketching approximations.
literature_snapshot.text: Frozen source synopsis, not a full-text copy. Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching, sections 2 and 3, studies squared-error fitting with a quadratic coefficient penalty and selection of regularization through held-out/cross-validation error. The closed-form ridge solution depends on the feature covariance and regularization strength. The paper discusses validation bias in a high-dimensional asymptotic regime. It does not identify an optimal polynomial degree or alpha for this task; those must be measured from the supplied public training and validation data. Mathematical facts are literature context, not local experimental evidence.

literature_snapshot.title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
literature_snapshot.abstract: Specialized agents perform literature review, planning, code experimentation, interpretation, and research reporting.
literature_snapshot.text: Literature claim from Agent Laboratory section 3: experiments execute generated code; an LLM reward model guides code selection. Its section 5 discusses self-evaluation and hallucinated results. This is not independent evidence of task performance here.

literature_snapshot.title: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
literature_snapshot.abstract: Agent laboratories share and retrieve prior reports using a local preprint server and similarity-based retrieval.
literature_snapshot.text: Literature claim from AgentRxiv section 3: agents retrieve reports through a SentenceTransformer similarity search. Section 4.1 reports hallucination/reward-hacking risks and human checking of experimental outputs. Retrieved reports require verification before adoption.

pilot_design.purpose: Initial paired variation estimate and interface verification before independent confirmatory sample-size design.
pilot_design.regime_coverage: Linear, quadratic and small-sample noisy development tasks cover different feature complexity and noise conditions.
pilot_design.repetitions_basis: The current independent variance-design criterion requires relative standard error 0.5 for the variance estimate: ceil(2 / 0.5**2) + 1 = 9 paired observations. Three preregistered development regimes each contribute three distinct seeds. These nine units are a pilot design requirement, never a cap on research loops; final sample count is independently calculated after complete reviewed paired observations.
pilot_design.seed_policy: Nine distinct fixed seeds prevent intentional reuse of the same pseudorandom x/noise stream across regimes: linear7/11/19, quadratic31/43/59, noisy71/89/107. B and C use the same data/seed within each pair. Distinct-seed units are treated as independent observations for the declared variance design; this is a statistical design assumption, not a measured proof of probabilistic independence. Existing unmatched development observations are never transplanted.
pilot_design.stopping_criteria_status: No absolute validation threshold is supplied in any unit or the shared envelope. This matches the planned final public contract: B performs its preregistered original phases; C uses a first verified anchor, evidence-based candidate comparison and memory, then stops if no justified fresh candidate remains or the same preregistered per-unit resource envelope is exhausted. The goal objective is to minimize public validation MSE; hidden test outcomes are scored only by the independent owner.
pilot_design.failure_policy: Preserve model/CPU failures, pending independent report reviews and unknown actions; no unsuccessful unit may be silently replaced.
pilot_design.final_status: Not a final evaluation and not an adoption claim.
pilot_design.policy_alignment: The earlier unmatched development criterion .03 and proposed but unexecuted .03/.6 pilot targets are not the stopping policy of this preregistered paired pilot or final suite. No result was observed under those proposed pilot settings. Explicit medium reasoning is also matched in both arms; old default-effort development results remain separate.
